title: Keystep holdout scratchpad — multi-turn fidelity checks
content:
Purpose: quick personal log for a small holdout test that keeps drifting in prod-like sims. Not polished — notes to self + examples + quick hypotheses.

Context / problem statement
- We've been seeing subtle output collapse in multi-turn assistant flows when prefix/KV cache is used heavily and the request sequence length varies. Apparent symptom: earlier, correct instruction-following on a user step gets overwritten by later context in inconsistent ways.
- Repro surface: medium-length sessions (6–12 turns) with instruction edits mid-session. Seems more visible on quantized model variants and on low-batch, low-latency routes.

Quick checklist to repro locally
- Model variant: rwd-open-7b-ql8 (also reproduced on 13b-4bit sim)
- Runtime config: prefix_cache=enabled, cache_ttl=180s, batch_size=1 (continuous batching minimal), use_kv_sharding=false
- Client: simulated UI that edits system prompt mid-session (turn 4).
- Metric to watch: token-level KL drift vs. reference baseline, and instruction adherence score (rudimentary).

Session sample (input -> model response) — redacted/simplified
1) User: "Plan a 3-day itinerary for Kyoto focused on food."
   Model: Useful 3-day plan (OK)
2) User: "Add budget options and transit tips."
   Model: Adds details (OK)
3) User: "Wait—actually make it family-friendly and remove nightlife suggestions."
   Model: Adapts, removes nightlife (OK)
4) Agent (system edit): "System: prioritize kid-friendly activities and reduce walking time."
   User continues: "Also include toddler-friendly restaurants."
   Model (observed regression): Reintroduces a late-night izakaya suggestion on Day 2.

Notes on the sample
- The reintroduced izakaya mention is a short span hallucination: not present in prior tokens but appears after the cache refresh at turn 4.
- Hypothesis: stale KV entries from earlier 'food' tokens get incorrectly scored higher after system prompt edit; scoring/attention mask interplay may cause a short burst of high-prob tokens unrelated to updated system instruction.

Quick experiments run (timestamps local)
- 2026-01-07 10:30: toggled cache_ttl 0 (disable) -> regression disappears in sim but tail latency + token cost increases ~6%.
- 2026-01-09 14:12: set cache_merge_policy="conservative" (deprecate long-range prefix reuse) -> regression reduces but still present in ~1/50 sessions.
- 2026-01-13 09:40: quantized vs fp16 comparison -> quantized shows 2.3x higher incidence of the izakaya reappearance.

Hypotheses (ranked)
1) KV scoring bug: when system prompt changes mid-session, the runtime isn't invalidating or reprioritizing certain KV entries, so earlier culinary tokens leak into generation via stale attention keys. This would explain stronger effect in quantized kernels (different numeric dynamics).
2) Prompt concatenation error: the token indices used for prefix/cache mapping get off-by-one after an insert/edit, causing an unaligned KV read for a short window.
3) Sampling-temperature interaction: small temperature (0.2) combined with biased logits from old KV leads to deterministic reappearance in low-entropy routes (why batch_size=1 worse).

Quick triage commands to run next
- Run reproducer with kv-trace enabled (capture KV keys/values around edit boundary). Tag logs with session id.
- Add controlled noise to logits after cache read (tiny epsilon) to test if determinism reduces reappearance — cheap A/B.
- Run a micro experiment with batch_size=4 to see if continuous batching masks or amplifies; schedule on dedicated pool due to cost.

Eyes-only debugging notes
- Check PR 212 (linked) — previous attempt to change cache_merge_policy introduced an odd fallback in kernel selection for ql8 paths. Could be related.
- Jira JIRA-ML-4873 has user reports with similar keywords: "reintroduced nightlife". Cross-linking to support tickets may help customer triage.

Small ad-hoc rubric (for quick manual triage) — simple 0/1/2 scoring per session sample
- 0 = baseline correct (no contradicting suggestions; respects system edit)
- 1 = minor drift (mentions acceptable but tangential items — not dangerous)
- 2 = clear contradicting reintroduction (explicitly undoes system instruction like reintroducing nightlife)

Recent annotated samples (hand-labels) — 40 cases
- 28 -> score 0
- 9  -> score 1
- 3  -> score 2 (the izakaya reintro appears in all 3)

Immediate next steps (short):
- Enable kv-trace on a small canary group and collect 200 failing/successful sessions. (assign to Omar)
- Run the epsilon-logit-noise microtest (I can schedule a cheap run).
- Try forcing cache invalidation on system-prompt-edit events in the client to confirm mitigation surface. If mitigation works, file a small runtime hotfix.

Longer-term thinking (notes):
- Might need a standard for "session-edit" events that guarantees cache invalidation or remapping semantics across runtimes. Could be a surface in Redwood Console (rollout toggle).
- Evaluate whether quantization numerics need a conservative KV-pruning strategy by default (cost vs safety tradeoff).

Random notes / TODOs to self:
- Capture 5 full KV dumps from a failing 13b sim (large) before deleting temporary logs.
- Sync with Maya on Friday to see if UX edit events in web client send the right metadata to server (timestamp/sequence id).
- If we push a short-lived client-side mitigation, include telemetry to show % reduction over a week.

End of scratchpad — will tidy later into a short PR description if we pin down root cause.

---

- 2026-01-13: quantized comparison added
